name: Isla Osei
life: “I sold work suits in a store that paid us too little to buy one.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the foot of Harbor Viaduct, where Isla pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I wanted to sell him a full suit on credit. I tore the form up when I saw how carefully he budgeted.
appearance: Isla has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Look for short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a soft blue checked shirt with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. In conversation Isla starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak.
personality: Isla is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Isla is concerned.
agenda: To offer fitting work a customer can afford this week.
family: Byron Felix is Isla’s cousin. Isla saves a place. Byron chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *A room for a father*, Byron says, “I wrote his prescriptions on separate cards.”
connections: Gale Levin. They decide which expensive additions the applicant can decline.

reactions.situation: Somebody offers to buy a complete suit for the applicant
reactions.response: Isla asks the applicant whether a whole donated suit would actually be welcome.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: Isla tells the stranger when the next opening is, then stays with the neighbor until their turn comes.
